A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWG research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-sampling experiments, D4RL returns, weight and guidance-scale ablations, and inference-time measurements in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds SWG-R evaluations across the D4RL tasks in Table 2.

M1.justification: v2 adds SWG-R, which generates a batch of candidate actions and selects the highest-weight action using the separate learned weight model. v1 suggested resampling but explicitly reported experiments without it. This is a limited inference extension; the joint diffusion model, training objective and core guidance procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 20 D4RL tasks across Locomotion, Ant Maze, Adroit Pen and Franka Kitchen, and the same six toy distributions. The eight-Gaussian example moves from v1 Appendix E into v2's main text; it is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains CQL, IQL, SfBC, IDQL, Diffuser, D-QL, D-DICE and QGPO, including their task-specific availability. The added SWG-R column evaluates the paper's own resampling variant; no external comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an inference-time candidate-batch search over M in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} for SWG-R (Appendix B.2). The retained SWG experiments keep their preprocessing, training budgets, architectures, diffusion steps, guidance-scale search and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The new SWG/SWG-R comparison tests the effect of adding action resampling across D4RL. Existing weight, guidance-scale and network-scaling analyses remain unchanged. In particular, v2 Section 6.4 reproduces the guidance-scale study already present in v1 Appendix D.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 2 means and standard deviations over five seeds, and timing means with two-standard-deviation bands over 10,000 runs. SWG-R follows the existing reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds SWG-R results for all 20 tasks, with group averages of 78.8, 80.3, 97.4 and 70.2 for Locomotion, Ant Maze, Adroit Pen and Kitchen, respectively. The retained SWG averages are 75.5, 75.1, 70.4 and 67.4. These are results for the added resampling setting; all original SWG and baseline numbers remain unchanged. The addition substantially expands the main empirical evidence.

T1.justification: The extraction definition, Proposition 3.3, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged. However, v1 Appendix C.2's short mathematical reduction of conditional sampling to weighted sampling, using w(a,c) proportional to q(c|a), is removed.

C1.justification: The central claim of exact guidance from a joint action–weight diffusion model is retained. v2 reframes the experimental contribution as a proof of concept, explicitly conditions competitive D4RL performance on resampling in the abstract, and adds the demonstrated benefit of SWG-R to its contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the limitations beyond weaker benchmark performance: changing guidance requires retraining, joint action–weight learning may require greater capacity, and mixed-action datasets expose weaknesses attributed to weights or architecture. It also identifies resampling's expanded search cost and removes v1's dismissal of Locomotion as a saturated, potentially untrustworthy benchmark.

D1.justification: v2 documents SWG-R's candidate-batch search and clarifies that selection uses the separate expectile-weight model. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, training-time and repository information is retained. Weight-ablation implementation details promoted into Section 6.3 were already disclosed in v1 Appendix D.4.

R1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix B's broader related-work survey, including discussions and citations concerning Transformers, VAEs, classifier-free guidance and accelerated diffusion sampling. It also drops the conditional-guidance comparison and D5RL citation. The direct CEP/D-DICE comparison survives as Section 4, but the overall research context is substantially narrower.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: the guidance-method comparison moves into a main section, guidance sensitivity and weight-ablation details move into the main experiments, and the appendices are consolidated. The abstract, experimental narrative and conclusion are revised around SWG-R, alongside widespread language and citation-style editing.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different publication layout, adds the method-comparison schematic in Figure 1, expands Table 1 with loss functions and Table 2 with SWG-R, and redistributes toy panels across main-text and appendix figures. Guidance-sensitivity tables also move into the main text. The existing toy plots and timing curves are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 turns the previously suggested resampling extension into a measured SWG/SWG-R comparison, ties the abstract's performance claim to resampling, and explains important intrinsic limitations and tuning costs. These improve evidential support and transparency. The gains remain limited: the core theory and original experiments are unchanged, broader related-work coverage is reduced, and the added resampling setting lacks a corresponding inference-cost analysis.
